In Chinese culture, it's considered unlucky to hang clothes or towels outside to dry during the Chinese New Year, especially on the first few days. This is because the Chinese word for "towel" (, fú) sounds similar to the word for "fortune" or "good luck" (, fú). Hanging a towel outside to dry might be seen as a way of "washing away" good fortune, which is considered taboo during this festive period. So, to avoid any potential bad luck, it's best to hang the towel to dry indoors or use a drying rack.
